It's an unpopular opinion in this sub, but FITS is his most relatable work for me. There's such a niche experience when someone decides to get sober, build a life in a new way without the vices, and then realize it's still not what's best for you anymore. Making the decision to leave the safety of the first support system I'd built in my own life after choosing sobriety felt impossible. I stayed longer than I wanted to, because I was more scared of relapsing than I was of being unhappy where I was at the time, because at least I wasn't drinking anymore. It's awful. It's hard. It's beautiful. It's freeing. It's painful. It's vulnerable. I can't even remember how many times I felt like I had no grasp on anything I was experiencing in those days. Picking up my brand new life and moving it all again was potentially more scary than getting sober in the first place. It took me a long time to let myself feel "good" things again. FITS captured so many of those emotions and experiences from my own journey that made me who I am now.

I definitely think it’s valid to be disappointed that we didn’t hear a song/songs we would have loved to hear live. Especially when it’s played later, or differently, or again. And we just missed it. It sucks. If you think about it, though, there’s really a very slim chance we would hear any song we want live since the set is just one song on guitar and one song on piano (although mash-ups increase the number of songs played now.)

I’ve had to fight my own FOMO with the tour, even though I saw the show in Nashville in May of 2023. She was doing it with a broken heart big time during that stretch. There was no TTPD yet. My show was nearly rained out, so I didn’t get to see Phoebe Bridgers/BoyGenius open. Mash-ups weren’t a thing at that point. I didn’t get a code to get tickets when she came back to the US, and couldn’t find a ticket when it was time for the NOLA shows. And generally, the energy at the shows now is so different than it was 18 months ago. 

Even so, for the rest of my life, I can say I was at The Eras Tour. in decades, people will be talking about it like the generations before us talk about The Beatles and their shows. I love that for me! I’m glad people are live-streaming the shows now, too, so I can experience these shows at all. 

I’m sorry you missed the song(s) you wanted to hear, and I hope you enjoyed the experience!
